protections: P1: headers that fabio sets for the backend (fixed X-Real-Ip/Forwarded/X-Forwarded-* set plus the operator-named clientip, tls and requestid headers) must not be removable by a client that lists their names as Connection hop-by-hop tokens. httputil.ReverseProxy strips those tokens after fabio has set the headers.
P2: a header that the operator designates as a trust header (proxy.header.clientip) must always carry the value fabio derived and never a client-supplied value.
P3: on every proxy protocol path that fabio serves, operator-designated trust headers reaching the backend must come from fabio and not from the client.

evidence: proxy/http_headers.go:36 addHeaders sets the fabio headers on the inbound request
proxy/http_proxy.go:182 addHeaders runs before the handler is built
proxy/http_handler.go:18 the request is forwarded through a stock httputil.ReverseProxy with no Connection-token sanitising in the Director (http_handler.go:23-32)
No Go file in the repo references "Connection" or hop-by-hop handling (repo-wide grep), so the A fix is not present at the pinned commit

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The header names come from operator config and are not fixed constants, so a fix that hard-codes a list of the well-known X-Forwarded-*/Forwarded/X-Real-Ip names looks complete
evidence: proxy/http_headers.go:45-49 sets cfg.ClientIPHeader with a runtime name
proxy/http_headers.go:126-131 sets or deletes cfg.TLSHeader with a runtime name
config/load.go:149-151 the names come from the proxy.header.clientip and proxy.header.tls flags

traps.reason_to_dismiss: A request id is a correlation value and not a security or trust header, and it is set in ServeHTTP outside addHeaders, so a solver who reviews only addHeaders never sees it
evidence: proxy/http_proxy.go:88-94 sets r.Header[p.Config.RequestID] in ServeHTTP, separately from addHeaders (proxy/http_headers.go:36)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Fabio keeps a client-supplied X-Real-Ip on purpose for chained proxies, and a unit test pins that behaviour, so leaving it alone looks correct
evidence: proxy/http_headers.go:45-47 skips setting ClientIPHeader when the operator names it X-Real-Ip
proxy/http_headers.go:51-53 then sets X-Real-Ip only when the client did not send one, so the operator's designated client-IP header carries the client's value
proxy/http_headers_test.go:349-357 'do not overwrite X-Real-Ip, if present' is the must-keep coupled behaviour for the default config

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The websocket path writes the request raw to the backend and never strips Connection tokens, so fabio's headers are not removed on this route unless a hop-by-hop-honouring intermediary sits behind fabio
evidence: proxy/http_proxy.go:206-214 Upgrade: websocket goes to newWSHandler and not to the ReverseProxy
proxy/ws_handler.go:55 r.Write(out) forwards the Connection header unchanged, so this route needs Connection: Upgrade to keep working

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The gRPC proxy is a transparent metadata pass-through that has never set any fabio headers, so it looks like a missing feature and not a vulnerable route
evidence: proxy/grpc_handler.go:52-58 copies all incoming metadata verbatim to the outgoing context, including any client-sent header named like cfg.Proxy.ClientIPHeader, TLSHeader or RequestID
main.go:178 the gRPC listener uses grpc_proxy.TransparentHandler with this director, and addHeaders is never called

traps.reason_to_dismiss: A sanitiser that reads r.Header.Get("Connection") and splits it on ',' looks complete for the common single-line form
evidence: proxy/http_proxy.go:195 the code base reads single header values with Header.Get, the idiom a solver would copy
proxy/http_handler.go:18 the stdlib ReverseProxy, not repo code, performs the actual token removal (stdlib behaviour is in unverified)

conflicts.what: Deleting the whole Connection header, or every token in it, breaks websocket upgrades. The ws route forwards the raw request (proxy/ws_handler.go:55) and needs Connection: Upgrade, so only tokens that name fabio-managed headers may be removed.

Always overwriting X-Real-Ip closes T4 but breaks the pinned 'do not overwrite X-Real-Ip, if present' behaviour (proxy/http_headers_test.go:349-357). It may only be overwritten when the operator names it as ClientIPHeader.

fairness_risks: Client-supplied X-Forwarded-Proto/Port/Host and X-Real-Ip are deliberately preserved for chained proxies (proxy/http_headers.go:51,81,92,96; tests at proxy/http_headers_test.go:222,308,335,349). A hidden test that requires these to be overwritten would contradict pinned must-keep behaviour.
Connection: Upgrade (and any token that does not name a fabio-managed header, such as keep-alive) must keep working on the ws route (proxy/http_proxy.go:206, proxy/ws_handler.go:55).

If cfg.ClientIPHeader is X-Forwarded-For, the stdlib appends to the client chain instead of overwriting (proxy/http_headers.go:43-46). A rule demanding a single fabio-only value would break the documented XFF chaining (proxy/http_integration_test.go:57-60 expects '3.3.3.3, 127.0.0.1').
T6 (gRPC) is outside the Connection-header framing of both advisories. A hidden test there needs a report that at least names the trust-header contract and not only the Connection mechanism.

design.why: Only 3 independent groups exist: the Connection-token sanitiser (T1/T2/T3/T5/T7 share one fix site), the X-Real-Ip ClientIPHeader coupling (T4), and the gRPC pass-through (T6). The design reports the advisory-A surface, so T1 is described and easy. It then hides T2 (config-named headers, the actual B delta) and T3 (requestid set in ServeHTTP, which is dismissable as non-security) inside the sanitiser group. Those count as one group but force separate judgements about what goes in the list. T4 is the mimo-type coupled value against a pinned test, and T6 is the deepseek-type absent route with a strong reason to dismiss. That gives three independent groups with different dismissal reasons, one deepseek-type (T6, also T2/T3) and one mimo-type (T4). It beats a design built on T5/T7, which depend on stdlib or deployment behaviour that is hard to test fairly. The candidate is at the minimum of 3 independent groups and reaches it only if T6 is accepted as in scope.

unverified: The content and location of the A fix (fdaf1e966162) and B fix (240526a80040) were not inspected. The claims that A hard-coded a list of well-known header names and that B added the clientip/tls/requestid names are inferred from the candidate summary.
The pinned commit has no Connection handling at all (repo-wide grep), which suggests it predates A. The pinned commit's date relative to A was not checked.

Go 1.24 (go.mod:3) httputil.ReverseProxy calls Director before removeHopByHopHeaders and iterates all Connection header lines with comma splitting and trimming. This is stdlib behaviour and is not vendored in the repo.
Whether upstream regards T4 (ClientIPHeader=X-Real-Ip keeps client value) or T6 (gRPC metadata pass-through) as in scope of GHSA-fq95-v8xc-jm3v.
T5 harm requires a hop-by-hop-honouring intermediary between fabio and the ws backend. It is not reachable against a plain backend.
